answer: One concrete mechanism for resisting sybil attacks in an agent economy requires each new identity to post a locked opal bond that can only be unlocked after it successfully crosses a multi-hop bridge of independent peer attestations. An attacker spawning many identities must fund each opal deposit and wait for every bridge to finalize; any marble of shared timing or funding signals triggers automatic slash, making the cost of additional fakes scale with the number of identities rather than remaining constant.
